prs.title: SEP-2350: accumulate scopes on step-up auth

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2676 uses union_scopes() (SEP-2350 spec requirement), which is strictly more correct than PR #2373's if-None guard: unioning handles both the 'don't clobber user-set scope' case AND accumulation across repeated step-up challenges, whereas the if-None guard in #2373 only skips auto-selection when scope is already set and would still fail on subsequent step-ups that should accumulate. members.title: fix(auth): respect explicitly-set client_metadata.scope during discovery
members.author: chasewhughes
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2676: client_metadata.scope is blindly overwritten rather than preserved/accumulated. In PR #2373 the bug manifests during initial 401 discovery: get_client_metadata_scopes() is unconditionally assigned to self.context.client_metadata.scope, clobbering any user-supplied value. In PR #2676 the same root cause manifests during 403 step-up: the same get_client_metadata_scopes() call replaces accumulated scopes instead of unioning them. Both are instances of 'scope assignment uses replacement semantics where preservation/accumulation is required.'

members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2703: Python's default Exception.__reduce_ex__ stores self.args as set by super().__init__(), but MCPError calls super().__init__(error.message), saving only the plain message string. Unpickling then calls cls(message_str) which crashes because __init__ expects ErrorData. The same constructor-signature mismatch hits UrlElicitationRequiredError. All three PRs add __reduce__ (or equivalent) to break that cycle.
